summary: Today's decisions hold up after the close. I approved one $10 BND buy and rejected INCY. BND filled at $71.298 on 10-28, in line with the expected fill near $71.3, and sits at -0.29% ($39.86, 6.6% of equity). That is a small loss on a day when the Fed decision was still pending, and it says nothing about the call either way. The invalidation of a BND close below about $70.0 is 1.8% under the fill, so L1 was applied correctly. INCY was rejected because its estimated 10-27 earnings date had passed with no 8-K 2.02 or results headline, which pointed to an imminent print. A $12 buy could not be protected by a closing-price stop against a gap. The outcome cannot be judged yet, because INCY's results are still unverified and it is not in today's close data. Account equity is $601.40 (+0.23% since 10-20) against SPY +0.76%, with a drawdown of 0.52%. The lag comes mainly from holding about 11.7% cash and a 26% staples lean in a day when SPY rose. One day does not say the reasoning was wrong. The book is still not fully invested, but I judged that deploying more into Fed day and mega-cap earnings was not required. The real review comes after the Fed and the Microsoft and Alphabet prints. Open items: DPZ is -2.25% and its invalidation ($274.88) is still anchored to the pre-fill reference close and sits about 13% under the $316.58 fill, so L1 remains unfixed there. IDXX has its print around 11-02 after two PT cuts. KR fell 1.29% today with no news.
lessons: Re-anchor existing invalidations to the actual fill when reviewing held positions. DPZ's $274.88 stop is still about 13% under its fill and has now been flagged on several reviews; the next PM pass should restate it (about $285 for a 10% stop from $316.58) rather than carry it forward.

When an estimated earnings date has passed with no 8-K 2.02 or results headline, treat the print as imminent rather than absent (L2). Rejecting a buy on that basis is cheaper than sizing small, because a closing-price invalidation cannot protect against an earnings gap. Revisit INCY only after it reports.

Bond weight (BND plus IEF) is now about 9% of equity, built over three buys in four sessions on one growth-scare thesis. Do not add further bond exposure without a post-Fed reassessment, as the BND thesis already states; the Skeptic's point that the price-based BND invalidation is hard to trigger should be answered with a concrete level next time, such as the 10-23 entry of 71.28 or a stated 200-day margin.

Health Care overlap should be sized as one sleeve (L3): IDXX is already 6.7% of equity with a print on 11-02 and a negative PT drift. Any new Health Care buy before that print adds correlated event risk, whatever the label differences between a diagnostics firm and a drug developer.
